subject: Accounting
title: Accounts Payable Tracking
description: A fast breakdown of Accounts Payable Tracking for builders.

hook.text: A supplier sends 30 invoices a month. Missing a payment deadline means late fees—or losing the supplier.

buildup.text: Accounts payable tracks what the business owes—invoices received, payment terms, and due dates.

discovery.text: Many suppliers offer early payment discounts—2% off if paid within 10 days instead of 30.

twist.text: Missing a 2/10 discount on a $100,000 invoice costs $2,000—the equivalent of 36% annual interest.

climax.text: Well-managed payables optimize cash flow by timing payments to capture discounts.

punchline.text: Pay on time. Pay early when the discount is worth it.

quiz.question: Why should businesses pay attention to early payment discounts?
options: Missing them can be equivalent to very high interest rates
They reduce the amount of goods received

details.summary: Accounts payable tracking manages the money a business owes to suppliers and vendors. This topic covers how to record payables, manage due dates, take advantage of early payment discounts, and maintain healthy vendor relationships.
details.whyItMatters: Poor accounts payable management leads to missed discounts, late fees, damaged supplier relationships, and inaccurate financial statements. Consistent tracking keeps cash flow predictable.
takeaways: Accounts payable is a current liability representing money owed to suppliers
Early payment discounts like 2/10 net 30 can save significant money annually
Aging schedules help prioritize which bills to pay first and spot overdue invoices

faq.question: What is accounts payable in bookkeeping?
faq.answer: Accounts payable is the total amount a business owes to suppliers for goods or services received but not yet paid for. It appears as a current liability on the balance sheet and must be tracked carefully to manage cash flow and maintain vendor trust.

faq.question: What does 2/10 net 30 mean in accounts payable?
faq.answer: This payment term means the buyer gets a 2% discount if they pay within 10 days; otherwise, the full amount is due in 30 days. Taking these discounts consistently can save businesses thousands of dollars annually on supply costs.
